name: stri_split_fixed
title: Split a String By Pattern Matches

origin.description: Split each string on a literal delimiter.
origin.usage: stri_split_fixed(str, pattern, n = -1L, omit_empty = FALSE, tokens_only = FALSE, simplify = FALSE, ..., opts_fixed = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to split.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal delimiters. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. A negative value means every piece.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: TRUE drops empty pieces. FALSE keeps them. NA replaces them with NA.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If TRUE and n is positive, return at most n whole pieces and drop the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: FALSE returns a list. TRUE pads a matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

origin.details: str, pattern, n, and omit_empty are recycled together. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces and the remainder unless tokens_only is TRUE. An empty pattern or a missing string yields a one-element NA vector. An empty string is one empty piece, or nothing when omit_empty is TRUE. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
found <- stri_split_fixed("a_b_c_d", "_")
cat(paste0('stri_split_fixed("a_b_c_d", "_") returns ', paste(found[[1]], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Split each string on a literal delimiter.
translation.usage: stri_split_fixed(str, pattern, n=-1, omit_empty=False, tokens_only=False, simplify=False, opts_fixed=None, case_insensitive=None, overlap=None)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Literal delimiter, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. A negative value means every piece. NA yields a one-element NA vector.

arguments.name: omit_empty
arguments.text: True drops empty pieces. False keeps them. NA replaces them with NA.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: If true and n is positive, return at most n whole pieces and drop the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: False returns a list of lists. True pads a matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

arguments.name: opts_fixed
arguments.text: None, or a dict of search settings. Overlap is ignored.

arguments.name: case_insensitive
arguments.text: If given, match the simple uppercase of each code point.

arguments.name: overlap
arguments.text: Ignored, as in the installed function.

translation.details: str, pattern, n, and omit_empty are recycled together. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces and the remainder unless tokens_only is true. An empty pattern or a missing string yields a one-element NA list. An empty string is one empty piece, or nothing when omit_empty is true. A missing opts_fixed uses case-sensitive search without overlap. A dict may set case_insensitive and overlap. Case-insensitive search maps each code point with ICU u_toupper. A character whose uppercase form is longer than one code point is left unchanged, so ß does not match SS.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings and NA, or a list of padded rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.fixed import stri_split_fixed
found = stri_split_fixed("a_b_c_d", "_")
print('stri_split_fixed("a_b_c_d", "_") returns ' + ", ".join(found[0]) + ".")
